eMLG, H, G, lambda, and E.5 all measure diversity of multilocus genotypes (MLG). Yes. You can add additional igraph plotting parameters as arguments to the plot_poppr_msn function. I would recommend using vertex.label.dist and/or vertex.label.degree (see the igraph documentation for details: http://igraph.org/r/doc/plot.common.html).

> Additionally,  what is the "convert to a genclone ?" option in the GUI for ? If my data is already a snpclone object, is this process necessary ?

No, the process is not necessary if your data is already snpclone or genclone. In fact, you can ignore it since it does nothing if the incoming object already is a genclone/snpclone object. This option is meant for those who have genind or genlight objects. It offers a small speedup since the calculation of MLGs only has to be performed once for genclone/snpclone objects.

Hope that helps,
Zhian

P.S. You may want to update to the new version of poppr so that the nodes in your MSN are scaled by area.

I haven't seen it before, but it's nice to see that people are writing their own tutorials :)

I believe this may be a mistake in copy+paste. There are three columns in the data; the first "column" is simply the row numbers, which is the output from R. You can find a tutorial on how to handle strata here: https://github.com/thibautjombart/adegenet/wiki/Tutorials and an example of using strata to examine population differentiation here: http://popgen.nescent.org/2015-12-15-microsatellite-differentiation.html

> So should I set mine up by each of the 3 species, with the following:
>
> ind pop hostplant
> 1 1 1
> 2 2 3

I would recommend for your strata to have four columns:

1. individual ID (this allows you to make sure your strata are in the same order as your data)
2. species
3. population
4. host

Moreover, I would additionally recommend to include meaningful names as opposed to numbers.

Hope that helps!
Zhian

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

> I have browsed the manual but I couldn't find how to calculate metrics of differentiation in poppr , and poppr.amova() is also not applicable for snpclone object. Is there a way to solve it ?

Unfortunately, calculating AMOVA on genlight objects is not currently possible in poppr [1]. I would recommend to use the pegas implementation like so:

library("pegas")
myDist <- bitwise.dist(myGenlight, percent = FALSE)
res <- pegas::amova(myDist ~ pop/subpop, data = strata(myGenlight), is.squared = TRUE)

Replace "myGenlight" with the name of your data and "pop/subpop" with the hierarchy present in your strata slot.

> Moreover, If I want to export my snpclone object which is MLG filtered, how should I code?

If you want to export the object for use in another Rscript, I would recommend using saveRDS() to save the object to a file and then readRDS() to read that file in a new session*. If you only need the MLG assignments, then he underlying genetic data does not change when you filter MLGs, so you can export the assignments as a CSV file along with your individual names and population data.

I hope that helps.

Zhian

[1]: https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/issues/72. This is not a simple problem and may still take a bit longer to implement as I am now only working on poppr in my spare time.
* If you defined your MLGs using a matrix, then you must also save that matrix and reload it with the same name.
